answer: The market accepts only identities issued by a contract that burns k(N+1) tokens per registration, where k>0 and N counts all identities ever issued. A farm with n aliases pays at least k(n+1) for the next; its first n cost at least kn(n+1)/2. The contract serializes registrations and never decreases N, so splitting wallets or resetting history cannot reduce fees. Pre-aging handles like falcon, quill, and lagoon requires paying successive fees upfront.
